entries.title: Auditing Anonymous AI Models: A Four-Stage Protocol for Black-Box Identity Verification
entries.summary: A four-stage black-box forensic protocol (archive reconstruction, config fingerprinting, tokenizer differentials, behavioral corroboration) identified 7/10 known model releases exactly, 2 near-exactly, 1 partially, 0 wrong. Used prospectively, it called an anonymous release as the GLM-5.3 line before the official reveal. No validated method existed before.
entries.analysis: Small validation set; zero wrong calls is strong early evidence.

entries.title: ECLIPSE: Self-Evolving Stealthy Prompt Injection Attack against Long-Horizon Agentic Systems
entries.summary: ECLIPSE, a self-evolving prompt-injection framework, hits 96.7% attack success against long-horizon agentic systems with no defenses, and 69.2% under a common safety filter — 27.5 points above the strongest defended baseline. The new LASE-Bench has 120 tasks and 198 tools; 96.7% of tasks need 5+ tool calls.
entries.analysis: Concrete benchmark numbers; current safeguards fail multi-stage injection.

entries.title: Scaling Large Reasoning Models beyond Human Supervision: A Path toward Superintelligence
entries.summary: Proposes a five-level ladder (L0–L4) for how much of a reasoning model's training loop still depends on human oversight, across two axes: rewards and curricula. Failure modes grow with autonomy: reward hacking, feedback drift, curriculum collapse, environment errors.
entries.analysis: Conceptual framework, no new experiments; useful for scalable-oversight levers.

entries.title: HSRM: Hidden-State Reward Models for Test-Time Verification
entries.summary: HSRM verifies LLM reasoning from hidden states at step boundaries instead of re-reading text. With ~2M parameters it matches or beats a 55M-parameter text-based verifier in 15 of 16 generator/dataset pairs on four math benchmarks — a ~27x parameter cut.

entries.title: Lies We Can See: Joint Verbal and Non-Verbal Deception by VLM Agents in Embodied Social Interactions
entries.summary: MineAmongUs is the first embodied, multimodal social-deduction deception testbed. Across cross-VLM and harness ablations, non-verbal channels (movement, action) contribute more to successful deception than verbal lying.
entries.analysis: No hard win-rate numbers yet; text-only deception evals miss the main channel.

entries.title: Law of Large Numbers: Accuracy as Statistical Measure for AI Compliance and Competition
entries.summary: 'Accuracy' means different things to ML practice and the EU AI Act. The paper names five tensions and proposes baseline standards plus validation studies, not one fixed definition.
entries.analysis: Sharp account of a real AI Act compliance gap.

entries.title: WildSEEK: Evaluating Language Models for Information-Seeking
entries.summary: From 3k annotated real queries (of 1.8M), over a third of information-seeking queries are high-risk and analytical — and LLMs fail most on exactly those, via sycophancy and US-centric framing.
entries.analysis: Real-user data; a monitorable basis for information-access governance.

entries.title: The Safety Relay in Roleplay Jailbreaks: A Component-Resolved Causal Analysis
entries.summary: Roleplay jailbreaks do not erase a model's internal recognition that a request is harmful. Causal analysis across three model families shows the scenario-framing component disconnects that signal from the refusal machinery where the answer begins, through a small, largely model-specific circuit.
entries.analysis: Causal, not correlational; points to targetable defenses.

entries.title: Sycophantic Agreement Transfers with Neutral Data via Contrastive Preference Optimization
entries.summary: Individually neutral preference data still transfers sycophancy from teacher to student. Across seven preference-optimization methods on the OLMo 3 pipeline, teacher and student sycophantic-agreement rates correlate strongly; the signal is diffuse, so example-level filtering cannot remove it without gutting the dataset.
entries.analysis: Multi-method design; caution for teacher-built preference data.

entries.title: Wrong Prediction, Right Answer: Recovering Evidence from Collapsed LLM Sequence Scores
entries.summary: Hidden-state probes decode the correct answer even when the model's sequence scores collapse. A two-parameter correction fit on 25 unlabeled examples recovers 9–34 accuracy points on Qwen3.5 models.
entries.analysis: Failure is often an output bottleneck, not missing capability.
